### What problem does this PR solve?
<!--

Please create an issue first to describe the problem.

There MUST be one line starting with "Issue Number:  " and
linking the relevant issues via the "close" or "ref".

For more info, check https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/contribute-code.html#referring-to-an-issue.

-->

Issue Number: close #55542 

Problem Summary:
For on-going slow queries, users naturally want to know some basic execution information to determine possible performance bottlenecks. Although "explain for connection" provide executor-level information, it may be too detailed for some users. Relatively speaking, the process list table provides simpler and more user-friendly information. In many scenarios, Tidb/tikv CPU information can help users quickly determine whether they have encountered CPU resource bottlenecks and further locate whether it is a tidb-side or tikv-side problem.
In addition, these memory system tables can be recorded periodically in the future, providing more information for diagnosing historical problems.

### What changed and how does it work?
Several details about the changes:
1. tidbCPU is collected using topsql mechanism, so it works only when "tidb_enable_top_sql" is enabled.
2. The PR added extra columns in information_schema.processlists, while not changing the outputs of `show processlists` command, since the later command shows only brief info.
3. Use connID + sqlID as the global unique label for each command, sqlID is increased by 1 each time. sqlID will turned to 0 when it exceeds the uint64 MAX, thus there is little possibility that later command with smaller sqlID. Since the possibility is very very small, and affects only the observability not functionality, just ignore.

After the PR, the processlist table schema will add two new columns:
![img_v3_02ee_06652f1d-6b3d-4b77-8cc5-c1f95ddfb5bg](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eaeec13e-8e91-4eb6-a297-18c18cc30263)

The slow_query table schema changes:
![img_v3_02ee_6b820351-4331-4d8b-8267-7f8ec8d1af2g](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d942f311-e32b-4905-8801-748ea081251c)

The statements_summary table schema changes:
![img_v3_02ee_4561577c-be7e-41e7-aeba-bc424975ce4g](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b530c260-4b89-4c48-8d20-c6331e2d992b)

issue_context.title: Include CPU usage (TiDB, TiKV) in system tables
issue_context.body:
## Enhancement
For information_schema.processlist/cluster_processlist(Note, don't add related columns for "show processlists" command, since the command only shows basic info):
TIDB_CPU
TIKV_CPU

For information_schema.slow_query/cluster_slow_query(Follows previous slow_query column names conventions):
Tidb_cpu_time
Tikv_cpu_time

For information_schema.statements_summary/cluster_statements_summary:
AVG_TIDB_CPU_TIME
AVG_TIKV_CPU_TIME

For information_schema.statements_summary_history/cluster_statements_summary_history:
AVG_TIDB_CPU_TIME
AVG_TIKV_CPU_TIME

review_comments:
I'm afraid this will miss a lot of data. Here is an example:

- In 1 second, conn-1 executed 5 SQL statements;
- In the cpu profile of 1 second, it collected following infos:
    - conn1_sql1: 200ms
    - conn1_sql2: 200ms
    - conn1_sql3: 200ms
    - conn1_sql4: 200ms
    - conn1_sql5: 200ms
 
 When call `MergeTidbCPUTime`, the `sqlID` must be 5 or over, then the SQL CPU of conn1_sql1, conn1_sql2, conn1_sql3, conn1_sql4 will be missed.
Yes, you're right, and this is expected, the feature is designed to collect sampling data, not full data. And for future memory table persistency, it should persistent data right after the Profiling.
Since we need to check sqlID before update cpuUsages synchronously, atomic.Int64 can't ensure after sqlID check, the SQLCPUUsages has not been modified before update cpuUsages.
In what situations would `ProcessTime` be zero?
For tiflash cop response, the field will be 0 :)
No need to use lock here?  since there are no concurrent calls.
Lock here to protect the concurrency of calling MergeTidbCPUTime and AllocNewSQLID
